cdc_evaluation_guidelines: Alerts receive early-warning credit only when they satisfy the predefined event-matching and useful-action criteria. Unmatched alerts are reported separately.
Predefined criteria specify eligible pre-onset lead window (<= 2 days prior to onset), matching hazard, and matching geography before evaluation.
Forecast replay inputs must strictly reflect forecasts available at decision time without lookahead.
Observation-time detection delay (data date) and issue-time detection delay (operational alert dispatch timestamp) are evaluated and reported separately.
Direct latency between source availability and alert issuance is calculated exactly (e.g. 10m 2s), without conflating daily batch cadence.
Environmental-only policy produces an environmental exposure watch without health corroboration.
In a null scenario with no reference event, unmatched alerts are reported as false alarms without claiming a true event was rejected.

environmental_only.operational_tradeoff_summary: Environmental exposure watch: triggers on physical threshold exceedance (Day 32 in gradual heat, Day 26 in abrupt shock); 0 unmatched alerts in null scenario, but lacks clinical or workforce corroboration.

health_only.operational_tradeoff_summary: Uncorroborated health anomaly: detects clinical surge on onset day (Day 31 in gradual heat, Day 26 in abrupt shock); vulnerable to non-environmental noise, generating pre-onset baseline false alarms and 1 unmatched alert in null scenario.

fused_corroborated.operational_tradeoff_summary: Fused corroborated warning: corroborates physical exposure with health/workforce impact; triggers corroborated warning on Day 32 in gradual heat (+1 day observation delay, ~2 day issue delay; post-onset detection) and Day 26 in abrupt shock (0-day delay); 0 unmatched warnings in null scenario.
